Grills doing indoors what grills are not supposed to do indoors. Then the cards come to you. THE JOB Take what we shot and make people stop scrolling. This role sits between production and post, which is why we call it the pre-editor. You have real creative authority over how the story gets told. Nobody hands you the answer. You find it in the footage and you argue for it. WHAT THE WORK LOOKS LIKE The first three seconds Build hooks landing before somebody's thumb finishes moving. No logo, no wind up, no setup shot. jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description_text: About the role We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help shape and build the next generation of our network automation platforms. Our challenge is one of scale, complexity and criticality. We operate a massive global network supporting PlayStation Network, spanning more than 40 interconnection locations and 20+ data centres worldwide. Operating infrastructure at this scale safely and efficiently requires us to move beyond specialist-driven workflows and individual automation tools toward reliable, declarative software platforms. You will help make that transition. You will work on software that turns complex network and infrastructure operations into reliable, API-driven and increasingly self-service capabilities. This includes building control-plane services, declarative APIs and intent-based controllers that manage production infrastructure safely and consistently across our global footprint. This is a Staff-level engineering role with significant technical influence. You will combine hands-on engineering with setting technical direction: defining architectures, solving complex cross-system and distributed-systems problems, writing designs, driving alignment with senior engineers and architects, and mentoring engineers across the team. Your work will directly influence how one of the world's largest gaming networks is operated and automated, while establishing engineering patterns and platforms that can be reused across multiple network domains and services. jobs.title: Research Intern, Frontier Agents (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About the Role The Agents team investigates how to build, align, and scale frontier AI systems that can tackle complex, multi-step tasks and workflows across text and speech, with a particular focus on agentic and scientific domains. Our work sits at the intersection of agent capabilities, human-computer interaction, and infrastructure—from designing post-training methods for agentic behavior to developing evaluation frameworks for open-ended tasks where traditional metrics fall short. As a research intern, you will work on problems at the frontier of agentic AI, where challenges in alignment, reliability, and scalability are deeply intertwined. Projects may involve developing new training recipes for self-learning and long-horizon reasoning, curating datasets for non-deterministic scientific and agentic tasks, studying failure modes in agentic behavior, or building infrastructure that enables agent operations at scale. You'll operate in a space where algorithmic innovation, dataset and interaction design, and systems work come together to push the boundaries of what AI agents can reliably accomplish. Responsibilities Research and implement novel techniques in one or more of our focus areas Design and conduct rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses Document findings in scientific publications and blog posts Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team Requirements Currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering

jobs.title: Research Intern, Inference (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About The Role The Inference Research team is dedicated to building the next generation of efficient, scalable, and reliable serving systems for large foundation models, directly contributing to the mission of advancing open and transparent AI. Our work operates at the critical intersection of cutting-edge model architectures, high-performance systems engineering, and deep hardware optimization. We focus on co-designing software, algorithms, and models to significantly lower the cost and latency of modern AI systems. As a research intern, you will dive into the complexities of distributed inference, compiler-aware optimization, and novel inference-time computation strategies (such as speculative decoding and phase-aware execution). You will be tasked with co-designing and implementing cross-layer optimizations across models, systems, and hardware, with a focus on areas like KV cache design and large-scale serving architectures. Projects aim to unlock unprecedented performance and scale for foundation models, enabling faster serving, larger model deployment (e.g., Mixture-of-Experts), and robust, reproducible evaluation under realistic serving workloads.
